tests.name: Phalenâ€™s Test
tests.procedure: Patient flexes both wrists maximally (dorsal surfaces pressed together) and holds position for 60 seconds.
tests.positiveImplication: Numbness, tingling, or pain in median nerve distribution (thumb, index, middle finger) indicates CTS.
tests.negativeImplication: No sensory changes after 60 seconds of maximal flexion.

tests.name: Tinelâ€™s Sign
tests.procedure: Examiner taps lightly over median nerve at volar carpal tunnel using fingertip or reflex hammer.
tests.positiveImplication: Electric shock-like tingling sensation radiating into median nerve distribution indicates CTS.

tests.name: Carpal Compression Test (Durkanâ€™s Test)
tests.procedure: Examiner applies direct firm pressure with thumbs over carpal tunnel for up to 30 seconds.
tests.positiveImplication: Reproduction or worsening of paresthesias in median nerve territory confirms CTS.
tests.negativeImplication: No symptoms during 30 seconds of direct pressure.

tests.procedure: Examiner applies anteroposterior translation and stress forces to scapholunate, lunotriquetral, and collateral ligaments.

tests.name: Watsonâ€™s Test (Scaphoid Shift Test)

tests.name: TFCC Load Test
tests.procedure: Examiner places wrist in ulnar deviation, applies axial compressive load, and rotates forearm.
tests.positiveImplication: Pain, clicking, crepitus, or catching along ulnar joint line indicates TFCC tear.
tests.negativeImplication: Painless rotation under ulnar axial load.

tests.name: Press Test
tests.procedure: Patient uses hands to push up and support body weight from a seated position in a chair.
tests.positiveImplication: Reproduction of sharp ulnar-sided wrist pain upon axial loading suggests TFCC injury.

tests.name: Fovea Sign
tests.procedure: Examiner presses thumb into soft depression (fovea) between ulnar styloid and flexor carpi ulnaris tendon.
tests.positiveImplication: Exquisite focal tenderness in ulnar fovea indicates foveal avulsion of TFCC.

tests.name: Transillumination Test
tests.procedure: Light source applied directly against wrist swelling in a darkened room.
tests.positiveImplication: Light transmits brightly through the mass (transillumination), confirming fluid-filled cyst (ganglion).
tests.negativeImplication: Mass remains dark and opaque (suggests solid tumor or tenosynovitis).

tests.name: Palpation and Fluctuation Test
tests.procedure: Examiner palpates lump during full wrist flexion and extension.
tests.positiveImplication: Firm, well-circumscribed, smooth, mobile mass becoming more prominent with wrist flexion.
